title: Signed impulse estimates and global smooth solutions for finite multispecies relativistic Vlasov–Maxwell
strongest_supported_claim: The exact finite-species normalization, source/receiver pair identity, positive energy and retarded measures, conditional transfer mechanism, simultaneous closure and momentum-doubling implication, and continuation/localization arguments survived the checks performed. The global conclusion is supported conditional on the full uniform analytic estimates imported from pinned family 362.
exact_checked_claims: Fixed finite species; strictly positive fixed masses; arbitrary fixed real charges; nonnegative compact smooth phase data; smooth bounded-derivative L2 Maxwell data satisfying Gauss constraints.
Normalization f_a=m_a^3 F_a(x,m_a v); pair coefficient e_a e_b/m_a and source acceleration coefficient e_a e_b^2/(m_a m_b).
Positive mass-weighted particle energy and nonnegative electromagnetic-plus-particle cone flux persist for opposite charges.
Phase volume preservation and retarded label Jacobian d=1-n.u; dt/ds=d/D; combined Eulerian measure D dt f_b dy dv.
Generic signed pair decomposition and cancellation of source acceleration before absolute values; no extra receiver charge-to-mass factor inside a_t.
Species aggregate used as positive measure on disjoint labelled characteristics, not as a solution of a common scalar transport equation.
Inspected logical order of baseline occupation, signed direction counting, enhanced occupation, parameter-threshold absorption, and selected receiver multiplier control.
Endpoint restoration and strict bootstrap improvement with eta, M, A chosen before the momentum threshold.
Conditional harmonic momentum-doubling time bound remains valid if the maximizing species changes.
Bounded-momentum Sobolev continuation scope, BGP division/logarithmic derivative mechanism, and Coulomb-plus-vacuum localization allowing nonzero total charge.
